title: AI Control System for Fusion Energy
summary: Next Step Fusion reports that reinforcement learning controlled plasma parameters at DIII-D during 2023–24 and improved controller training. Energy benefits remain future-facing.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Next Step Fusion reports that reinforcement learning controlled plasma parameters at DIII-D during 2023–24 and improved controller training. The account provides no independent verification of these research results. Energy benefits remain prospective.
purpose: Improve plasma control for fusion research and future reactors.
system: Next Step Fusion reinforcement-learning plasma controller
deployer: DIII-D National Fusion Facility research program

ratings.reason: Next Step Fusion reports experimental plasma-parameter control at DIII-D and more efficient controller training. Commercial fusion output remains unestablished.
Reliable clean energy remains a future application; delivered energy and climate benefits are unknown.

ai_role.statement: A reinforcement-learning policy controls plasma parameters from sensor and actuator data, reducing dependence on intermediate reconstructions in the experimental controller.

evidence.citation: International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025). Project-submitted account, current as of June 2025. ITU provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use Case 13: AI Control System for Fusion Energy

produced_by: The account does not separately establish the conditions responsible for the benefit.
must_hold: Control evaluation within a fusion research facility

headline: Reinforcement learning controls fusion plasma
claim_basis: Sources: the makers' report. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
